label: Day 1
blurb: The first chapter opens at sunset. A great novelist speaks, a lamp is lit by the water, the city eats and sings, and 2027 arrives over Ashtamudi.

sessions.title: Why we still need stories
sessions.description: The opening conversation. The novelist from Mahé, whose Delhi: A Soliloquy won the JCB Prize for Literature, on a lifetime of stories and why they matter more than ever.

sessions.title: Lighting the lamp at sunset
sessions.description: The festival opens by the water as the sun goes down: a traditional lamp, a welcome from Kollam, and the first page turned.
guests: Festival hosts and guests of honour (to be announced)

sessions.title: The year in books
sessions.description: A lively, opinionated look back at the Malayalam and English books that defined 2026, and the ones to read next.

sessions.title: New Year’s Eve by the lake
sessions.description: Ouseppachan, who has scored Malayalam cinema since Kaathodu Kaathoram, leads an evening of songs with guest singers and the festival band.

sessions.title: Countdown on Ashtamudi
sessions.description: The countdown to 2027, together by the lake, with music and light, and the first minutes of the new year.

label: Day 2
blurb: New Year’s Day begins with poems at sunrise and becomes a day of great Malayalam storytellers: the novel, the short story and the films that grew from them. At night, Khasak opens.
allDay: Exhibition: Eight Arms, art on Ashtamudi · 8 Point Art Cafe · 10:00–20:00

sessions.title: First light: poems for a new year
sessions.description: Readings on the lakeside deck as the first sun of 2027 comes up over the water.
guests: Young poets of Kerala, chosen by open call

sessions.title: The Malayali in the mirror
sessions.description: The author of Manushyanu Oru Aamukham (A Preface to Man), winner of the Sahitya Akademi Award, on a novel that spans a century of Kerala life, and what it says about us.

sessions.title: From notebook to novel
sessions.description: A hands-on workshop for first-time writers with the author of the bestselling Ram C/O Anandhi. Limited places.

sessions.title: Short story, long life
sessions.description: Two masters of the form on why the Malayalam short story keeps reinventing itself, from Bhaskara Pattelar to Biriyani.

sessions.title: Meesha: a novel and its storm
sessions.description: The JCB Prize-winning novelist on writing Meesha (Moustache), the storm that met it, and what a novel owes its readers.

sessions.title: Story Boat: tales from the lake
sessions.description: Stories of fish, boats and monsoon ghosts for ages 6 to 12, with a drawing to take home.

sessions.title: Agnisakshi to Ore Kadal: the art of adaptation
sessions.description: The filmmaker known for bringing novels and plays to the screen on what to keep, what to let go, and how a book becomes a film.

sessions.title: Sketching the backwaters
sessions.description: Illustrators draw the lake live as the light changes. Bring a sketchbook and join in.

sessions.title: Kavi Arangu: poetry without borders
sessions.description: The Tamil poet and seven-time National Award-winning lyricist reads with Malayalam poets: two languages, one evening of verse.

sessions.title: Khasakkinte Ithihasam: opening night
sessions.description: O. V. Vijayan’s novel as immersive theatre, directed by Deepan Sivaraman: a world you walk into. Evening performance; exact time to be confirmed. Ticketed separately: ₹1,500, or ₹1,600 with a Festival Pass for all five days.

label: Day 3
blurb: A day about crossing over, into other languages, other lives and other art forms: translation, women’s writing, a film that broke loose, history for everyone, and a night that belongs to the young.
allDay: Exhibition: Eight Arms, art on Ashtamudi · 8 Point Art Cafe · 10:00–20:00

sessions.title: Murals and memory: a heritage walk
sessions.description: A morning walk through Kollam’s old quarters with the art historian, on temple murals, trade and the city’s layered past. Starts at 8 Point Art Cafe; places are limited.

sessions.title: Aalahayude Penmakkal, and after
sessions.description: One of Malayalam’s boldest novelists on women, faith, the land, and the lives her novels bring to the centre.

sessions.title: Publishers’ table: the future of the book
sessions.description: Paper, screens, audiobooks and translation: publishers on what readers want next, and how a new writer gets found.

sessions.title: Mahé, Delhi and the world
sessions.description: How a Malayalam novel travels: the author and his translators on carrying a language, its jokes and its silences, into English.
guests: The translators of Delhi: A Soliloquy (invited)

sessions.title: Jallikattu: when a story breaks loose
sessions.description: The director and the writer on turning the short story Maoist into Jallikattu, a film that ran wild across the world’s festivals.

sessions.title: Carry a poem across
sessions.description: Translate a Malayalam poem into English, or the other way, with working translators. No experience needed, just two languages.

sessions.title: Travancore, retold
sessions.description: The historian behind The Ivory Throne on queens, courts and the art of writing history that people actually want to read.

sessions.title: Poetry Slam: the heats
sessions.description: Three minutes, one mic, no mercy. College poets compete for a place in Monday’s final.

sessions.title: Khasakkinte Ithihasam: second night
sessions.description: The second of three performances at Ashramam Maidan. Evening performance; exact time to be confirmed. Ticketed separately: ₹1,500, or ₹1,600 with a Festival Pass for all five days.

sessions.title: Indie & Rap Night
sessions.description: The festival turns up the volume: Malayalam rap, indie bands and spoken word.
guests: Independent musicians and rappers from Kerala (invited)

sessions.title: Cinema by the lake: Jallikattu
sessions.description: An open-air screening on the lakeside, with English subtitles. Subject to screening rights.

label: Day 4
blurb: Journeys of every kind: to over a hundred countries, into silence, across a desert on film, and back through a thousand years of Kollam’s own history. Sunday ends with song, and Khasak’s final night.
allDay: Exhibition: Eight Arms, art on Ashtamudi · 8 Point Art Cafe · 10:00–20:00

sessions.title: Sunrise with Sri M
sessions.description: The author of Apprenticed to a Himalayan Master on walking, listening and the journey within, followed by a few minutes of shared silence by the lake.

sessions.title: The world is a classroom
sessions.description: The creator of Sancharam on travelling to over a hundred countries with a camera, and what Kerala can learn from the world.

sessions.title: Kerala murals: a hands-on workshop
sessions.description: Learn the lines, colours and stories of Kerala’s mural tradition, and paint a small panel to take home.

sessions.title: Quilon: the port that named a calendar
sessions.description: Kollam’s thousand-year story: the port Marco Polo called Coilum, traders from China and Arabia, and the Kollam Era that still dates the Malayalam calendar.

sessions.title: Aadujeevitham: sixteen years to film a novel
sessions.description: The director on bringing Benyamin’s novel of survival in the desert to the screen as The Goat Life, a journey that took sixteen years.

sessions.title: Kites over Ashtamudi
sessions.description: Make a kite from paper and bamboo, write a line of poetry on its tail, and fly it by the lake. Ages 6 and up.

sessions.title: Freedom to write
sessions.description: Three writers who have never been afraid of an argument, on courage, censorship and the reader’s right to disagree.

sessions.title: Reels & Short-Film Challenge: the shortlist
sessions.description: The best 60-second reels and short films made for the festival, on the big screen, with an audience vote.

sessions.title: Words for music
sessions.description: The lyricist and the composer on how a song is made, where the words end and the tune begins, with live performances of songs old and new.

sessions.title: Khasakkinte Ithihasam: final night
sessions.description: The last of three performances at Ashramam Maidan. Evening performance; exact time to be confirmed. Ticketed separately: ₹1,500, or ₹1,600 with a Festival Pass for all five days.

label: Day 5
blurb: The last day belongs to what comes next: a veteran of stage and screen, a masterclass for storytellers, the poetry slam final, the Khasak company in conversation, and three generations of writers closing the book, for now.
allDay: Exhibition: Eight Arms, art on Ashtamudi · 8 Point Art Cafe · 10:00–18:00

sessions.title: Morning ragas by the lake
sessions.description: A quiet start to the last day: violin and voice on the lakeside deck.

sessions.title: A life on stage and screen
sessions.description: From his father N. N. Pillai’s theatre to the centenarian he played in Pookkaalam: the actor on a lifetime of performing.

sessions.title: Screenwriting from books: a masterclass
sessions.description: How to read a novel like a screenwriter: structure, point of view, and the scenes that were never in the book. Limited places.

sessions.title: The art of the Kerala temple
sessions.description: The art historian on murals, wood carving and the stories painted on temple walls, and how to look at them.

sessions.title: Poetry Slam: the final
sessions.description: The best college poets of the festival face off for the KILF 2027 slam title.

sessions.title: After Khasak: the company in conversation
sessions.description: Three nights on, the director and the company on staging a novel that readers carry in their heads.
guests: Director Deepan Sivaraman and the Khasakkinte Ithihasam company (invited)

sessions.title: Three generations, one language
sessions.description: The closing conversation: three novelists from three generations on where the Malayalam novel came from, and where it goes next.

sessions.title: Closing the book, for now
sessions.description: Thank-yous, the slam champion’s winning poem, and a promise to meet again by the lake.

sessions.title: Songs of the shore
sessions.description: The closing concert: Kerala’s folk songs, boat songs and new sounds, under the open sky.
guests: Folk and fusion artists from Kerala (invited)
